summary: 24-year-old man assaulted, struck his head on the kerb: loss of consciousness ~2 min, vomited twice, GCS 12 (E3 V4 M5) on arrival, occipital boggy swelling.

inputs.hpi: Punched and fell backwards striking the back of his head on a kerb 1 hour ago. Knocked out for about 2 minutes per friends. Vomited twice since. Drowsy and repetitive. No anticoagulants. Had 4 beers.

exam.neuro: GCS 12, pupils equal and reactive 3 mm. Moves all limbs. No focal deficit. Boggy occipital scalp swelling. No CSF rhinorrhoea or otorrhoea, no Battle sign.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Traumatic brain injury (moderate, GCS 12) with loss of consciousness
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Moderate traumatic brain injury, GCS 12 with loss of consciousness and repeated vomiting after assault. CT head within 1 hour (NICE NG232), cervical spine imaging, neurosurgical discussion.

guideline.name: NICE NG232 — Head injury: assessment and early management
guideline.section: Section 1.4 (adults): CT head within 1 h for GCS <13 on initial assessment, GCS <15 at 2 h, suspected open/depressed or basal skull fracture, post-traumatic seizure, focal deficit, >1 episode of vomiting; CT within 8 h for people with no other indication who are taking anticoagulants (wording — "perform" or "consider" — to be checked against the 2023 text)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Head injury: assessment and early management (NG232). London: NICE; 2023.

guideline.name: ATLS 10th edition — head trauma
guideline.section: Chapter 6: GCS, pupils, prevention of secondary brain injury (avoid hypoxia and hypotension), CT head, early neurosurgical consultation; reverse anticoagulation in intracranial haemorrhage
guideline.citation: American College of Surgeons Committee on Trauma. ATLS Student Course Manual. 10th ed. Chicago: ACS; 2018. Chapter 6.

rationale: Base head-injury case meeting NICE NG232 1-hour CT criteria (GCS <13, more than one vomit). ICD S06.0X1A (concussion with LOC) is the code a clinician is likely to pick and tests the ICD route (the TBI protocol is registered as S09.9).
